topic: Noun as head of an ordinary NP
claim: The grammar argues for N-headedness from semantic selection and the distribution of bare NPs.
evidence_summary: Kim, money and women can each constitute an NP without an overt determiner.
finding: The distributional argument survives a challenge to selection as a sufficient head diagnostic.
inference: Can bare noun-headed NPs independently support the head analysis suggested by selection?

evidence.passage: §4, p. 357. The grammar argues for N-headedness from semantic selection and the distribution of bare NPs.
evidence.example: Compare Kim smiled, Money matters and Women voted (constructed). The head noun can form the subject NP without an overt determiner in each case. This is evidence beyond semantic selection by a verb.
evidence.establishes: The bare distribution supports CGEL’s ordinary noun-head analysis. Selection on its own would leave room for a different account of the nominal information available to a governor.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
